same_history_alpha_reallocation_is_not_c.exact_counterexample: Two independent valid e-values take 1/.045 with probability .045 and 0 otherwise. Choose (.045,.005) or (.005,.045) after seeing which channel is high. The selected-pair any-miscoverage probability is 1-.955^2=.087975 despite nominal alpha sum .05.
same_history_alpha_reallocation_is_not_c.finite_grid_relevance: The construction uses the two extreme members of the existing nine-allocation grid, so invalidity does not rely on continuum alpha selection.
same_history_alpha_reallocation_is_not_c.interpretation: Same-history alpha allocation requires a real selection correction; alpha1+alpha2=.05 is not itself a correction.

e_by_fcr_does_not_substitute_for_two_bou.derivation: When exactly two intervals are reported, FCR=E[V]/2 and P(V>=1)<=E[V]<=2 FCR. Thus strict pairwise SoS error <=.05 follows from FCR<=.025, not merely FCR<=.05. Under the direct 18-interval encoding of nine allocation pairs, e-BY with q=.025 and |S|=2 gives each selected interval alpha=.05/18, equal to uniform all-interval union insurance.
e_by_fcr_does_not_substitute_for_two_bou.guard: This is a statement about converting FCR into the stronger selected-pair any-miscoverage target, not a criticism of e-BY for FCR itself.

predictable_freeze_and_confirm_sos.theorem: At any pilot stopping time tau, choose/freeze one allocation pair using only F_tau. Restart both reporting e-processes at wealth 1 after tau. If their post-tau factors remain conditionally e-valid given F_tau and the selected pair, then conditional Ville plus a within-pair union bound yields selected-pair SoS error <=a1+a2<=.05. The number of candidate allocation pairs K disappears from the guarantee.
predictable_freeze_and_confirm_sos.benefit: This beats K-way all-pairs insurance in validity cost by replacing multiplicity insurance with fresh-confirmation/reset cost.
predictable_freeze_and_confirm_sos.cost: Pilot evidence cannot silently remain in the numerical reporting certificate. The method may therefore stop later than a fixed split when the pilot has already accumulated substantial useful evidence.
predictable_freeze_and_confirm_sos.log_e_planning_heuristic: Uniform K=9 insurance adds log 9 = 2.1972245773 nats to each selected channel threshold. Under a stationary growth approximation, resetting a channel has smaller remaining log-threshold than insured reuse when discarded pilot log-evidence is below log(1/pi_k). This inequality is not itself a valid post-hoc method-switch rule.

closed_testing_boundary_for_numeric_repo.public_method: Hartog and Lei show e-value closed testing can use weighted-average local e-tests and strictly improve on inverse-e weighted Bonferroni for fixed finite hypotheses.
closed_testing_boundary_for_numeric_repo.v3_projection_derivation: For two unrestricted numeric parameter families, rejecting a point null H1(theta1) under closure requires rejecting every intersection H1(theta1) cap H2(theta2) over nuisance theta2. With weighted-average local e-value w E1(theta1)+(1-w)E2(theta2), the worst nuisance uses m2=inf_theta2 E2(theta2). The required threshold is E1(theta1)>=(1/alpha-(1-w)m2)/w, also respecting the local threshold. If m2=0, this is exactly 1/(alpha w), the weighted-Bonferroni threshold. Thus fixed-hypothesis e-closure strength borrowing can disappear when projected to unrestricted marginal numeric CIs.
closed_testing_boundary_for_numeric_repo.example: At alpha=.05 and w=.5, if inf E2=0, closure requires E1>=40, identical to a .025 Bonferroni channel threshold. If inf E2 is only 1, the threshold is 39, only a small gain.
closed_testing_boundary_for_numeric_repo.interpretation: Closed testing remains promising for fixed decision nulls or constrained joint parameter regions, but it is not yet evidence of a free same-history improvement for two unrestricted marginal V3 reporting bounds.

selection_rule_aware_sos_status.known_positive_structure: Benjamini, Hechtlinger and Stark show SoS intervals can exploit known selection rules in specialized independent/top-k settings.
selection_rule_aware_sos_status.current_v3_gap: The V3 reporting selector is same-history, sequential and adaptively monitored; no matching conditional law/independence structure has yet been established that would justify importing those narrower SoS intervals.
selection_rule_aware_sos_status.current_portable_candidate: Predictable freeze-and-confirm is the first derived selection-aware construction here with a direct classical >=.95 selected-pair coverage proof and no K penalty.

public_evidence.title: Post-selection inference for e-value based confidence intervals
public_evidence.authors: Ziyu Xu; Ruodu Wang; Aaditya Ramdas
public_evidence.relevance: e-BY controls FCR under arbitrary selection/dependence and applies at stopping times; FCR remains distinct from strict selected-pair SoS.

public_evidence.title: Confidence Intervals for Selected Parameters
public_evidence.authors: Yoav Benjamini; Yotam Hechtlinger; Philip B. Stark
public_evidence.relevance: Known selection structure can reduce SoS conservatism in specialized independent/top-k models; not directly portable to adaptive V3 same-history selection.

public_evidence.title: Game-theoretic statistics and safe anytime-valid inference
public_evidence.authors: Aaditya Ramdas; Peter Grünwald; Vladimir Vovk; Glenn Shafer
public_evidence.relevance: e-processes/confidence sequences remain valid at stopping times and under optional continuation, supporting the post-freeze conditional e-process argument.

public_evidence.title: Family-wise Error Rate Control with E-values
public_evidence.relevance: e-value closure can strengthen fixed finite-hypothesis FWER tests via weighted-average e-values; numeric marginal-CI projection introduces a nuisance-envelope issue derived in this checkpoint.

measurement_validity_rules: A data-dependent reporting-alpha split is part of the statistical procedure, not a UI preference; if chosen from the same evidence, it must be covered by a selection-validity argument.
For a two-bound report, FCR=.05 is weaker than 95% simultaneous coverage of both selected bounds. State the target explicitly.
The portable no-K-penalty construction is selection on pilot history followed by fresh conditionally-valid confirmation; do not reuse pilot wealth in the reporting bounds without a separate proof.
Closed-testing power gains for fixed hypotheses do not automatically survive projection to unrestricted numeric marginal confidence intervals because all nuisance values must be protected.
Keep decision-only fixed-null alpha adaptation separate from numerical confidence-bound alpha adaptation; a rule safe for one need not be safe for the other.
scope_guards: The exact .087975 counterexample establishes existence of failure, not the failure rate of the deployed V3 selector.
The 200000-trajectory stress is synthetic and not production performance.

The closed-testing projection calculation is for weighted-average local intersection e-values; it is not an impossibility theorem for every conceivable selection-aware/conditional confidence construction.
The freeze-and-confirm theorem applies to post-selection evidence that is freshly conditionally e-valid; exact implementation on persisted V3 modules remains to be completed.
No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy or shared-ledger semantic input was used.
